newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--Spending on pharmaceuticals is increasing in Greece at a rate faster than GDP and now totals 40 percent of total spending on health, in contrast to an EU average of 9-18 percent.
--Cosmote - Greek telecoms organisation OTE's mobile phone subsidiary - is now in talks with Finland's Nokia over the 55 billion drachma contract for the DCS 1800 system.

--The European Commission is about to bring Olympic Airways down to earth, according to reports from Brussels. The Commission is reportedly prepared to tell OA that it must return 11 billion drachmas allocated for voluntary staff retirements to the state.
--The price of OTE's shares in its second public offer is now the epicentre of interest with today the day the price range is set for public subscription and book building, which ends on June 13.

--Seven months after the Delta financial scandal on the Athens bourse the report on 65 brokerage firms and subsequent decisions by the Capital Market Commission continue to be the focus of controversy on the market.
--There are growing hopes for a strong showing for OTE's second public offer, with the first orders coming in from Greece and abroad.

--State revenues in May increased at a rate of 19.9 percent according to the finance ministry, overshooting budget forecasts of 15.6 percent and leading to hopes that the budget will be executed this year without serious divergencies.
--The evaluation committee for the sale of Cretabank meets today to examine four offers, two from Chinese firms. A shortlist of three is expected today.
--OTE yesterday signed the contract to purchase a 20 percent stake in Serbia's PTT telecoms organisation, one of the most important telecoms agreements in the last few yers.
--Calm has returned to European money markets following ECOFIN's reassurance yesterday that Economic and Monetary Union would go ahead as planned.

--The state will file an injunction today against the consortium constructing the Athens Metro to remove Olympic Metro from the Syntagma-Keramikos work stations. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
